title: Pricing root soil-contact would bite — but as a flat tax, not a brake
question: A third of every root system is walled in at *every* size, so charging for it shrinks roots without stopping the blob. Do you want the cost anyway for the 51–79% spread it exposes, or does the brake have to come from somewhere else?
context_md:
You said: *"If the root cell isnt touching soil it cannot benefit the plant and has a cost ... not every plant root eventually grows into the same blob that is worst case."*

I measured whether that lever bites before anyone builds it — no root code written, `Absorb` is the plant-core lane's. Same two mature systems from the last card; the new numbers are the fraction of root cells sharing a **face** with soil (an exchange crosses a face, which is why transport is 4-neighbour and growth is 8).

| frames | root cells | touching soil | walled in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10,800 | 2,545 | 66.7% | 33.1% |
| 25,200 | 4,248 | 63.0% | 36.1% |
| 43,200 | 9,854 | 65.9% | 33.3% |

**Two things, and the second is the one that changes your proposal.**

1. **It is not a rounding error.** A third of every root system is already walled in by its own siblings — it can absorb nothing and cost carbon to build. Pricing that is real.
2. **But the fraction does not rise with size.** Root mass nearly quadruples between the first and last row and the interior stays flat at ~1/3. A solid disc would go the other way (interior share rises with radius), so what looks like a blob at zoom is actually a *dense branching mat* that keeps a constant surface-to-volume ratio at every scale. So the cost as specified is a **flat ~33% tax on root mass** — it makes roots cheaper overall, it does not make big ones disproportionately expensive, and on its own it will not stop the mass growing.

**The part that does support what you want** is the per-plant spread at 43,200 — the same eight plants, same genome, same scene:

```
  638 cells  51.3% touching       1427 cells  65.9%
  691 cells  61.8%                1731 cells  61.1%
  697 cells  57.5%                1861 cells  75.0%
  859 cells  79.2%                1950 cells  64.8%
```

One plant runs at 79% contact and another at 51% for the same carbon. That is already heterogeneous, and it is invisible today because contact is not priced — nothing rewards the efficient one. Pricing it would turn an existing spread into a fitness difference without forcing any shape, which is the "system, not preset" shape you asked for.

So my read: the cost is worth having for reason 2, but if the goal is specifically *stopping the blob*, something scale-dependent has to do that — a cap tied to the canopy it feeds, or crowding among a plant's own root tips the way the shoot already has crowding. I have not built or tuned any of it.
